children: Recognising women shaping India's legal profession across litigation, law firms, corporate legal leadership, academia, arbitration, mediation and legal tech.

The BW Legal World Compendium of Most Influential Women Lawyers in India recognises 326 women who are shaping the legal profession today. They are drawn from the courts, law firms, in-house legal teams, law schools, the arbitration and mediation community, and the legal technology ecosystem, and include both long-established leaders and a new generation to watch. The list is set out in eight categories. Detailed profiles of each honouree will follow in the next edition.
325 women across eight professional categories. Distinguished cohorts are identified within their relevant category and counted once.
Names are not arranged in order of ranking or seniority; within each bracket they run alphabetically by first name.
Pioneer, Hall of Fame and Trailblazer distinctions are defined within each category.

The Compendium of Most Influential Women Lawyers in India recognises women leaders across eight categories. Pioneer and Trailblazer distinctions are presented within the relevant category, alongside other professional cohorts, so that each individual is recognised in the context of her principal area of contribution.

This compendium is a curated selection, not a census. Any list of this kind will miss deserving names, and an omission is not a judgement on anyone's merit. There is a limit to how many profiles can be reviewed with care, and we chose a balanced number over an open-ended exercise that would never close.

Beyond our own research, the lists went through a layer of peer review. We consulted senior lawyers, legal professionals and retired general counsel. Some names came to us through self-nomination and others were nominated by peers. Where a placement was unclear, we referred it to senior members of the profession before deciding.

This edition builds on the 2024 edition, and the profiles of those featured will be published. We invite those not yet included to share their profiles for the next edition. This is a collaborative process, and each edition we strive to improve on the last.
